title: Sultanate of Cirebon
capsule: The Sultanate of Cirebon was an Islamic maritime state on the northern coast of West Java, traditionally founded by Sunan Gunung Jati (Syarif Hidayatullah), one of the Wali Songo (Nine Saints) credited with Islamizing Java, around 1482. Under Gunung Jati and his successors, Cirebon became a regional center for Islamic scholarship and trade, maintaining connections with Demak and later resisting Mataram encroachment. Internal succession disputes in the mid-seventeenth century led the sultanate to fragment into three sub-sultanates—Kasepuhan, Kanoman, and Kacirebonan—under Dutch VOC suzerainty, with formal Dutch overlordship acknowledged by treaty in 1677.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's political history is reconstructed primarily from Javanese court chronicles (babad) and Dutch VOC administrative records; territorial boundaries before 1677 are not precisely mapped.
